hints: Each move removes three coins total, so a+b must be divisible by 3.
Each move removes either one or two from either pile, so the larger pile cannot exceed twice the smaller.
Both conditions together are sufficient; check them per test case.
analogy: Each turn removes coins from both piles in a 1-to-2 ratio, so total size and balance limit whether emptying is possible.
example: For (2,1), the total is 3 and the piles fit the 2-to-1 balance, so one move empties them.
algorithm: For each case print YES exactly when (a+b)%3==0 and max(a,b)<=2*min(a,b).
correctness: If there are x moves of type (1,2) and y of type (2,1), then a=x+2y and b=2x+y. Solving gives nonnegative integers exactly under these two conditions.
complexity: O(1) time and O(1) extra space per test case.
